title: Edenbridge - reserved nodes + hybrid-burst discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery for reserved dedicated inference with hybrid burst to hosted. Key constraints: data residency for EU, SOC2+audit requirements, per-tenant isolation or dedicated tenancy for high-risk models, cost target under $0.002/token for high-throughput scoring, and desire to fail over to hosted Redwood for rare spikes. Action items assigned for telemetry and security artifact exchange.
topics: On-prem / VPC option and region residency
action_items: Owner: Tom Reeves; Item: Share 30/90/95 percentile token volumes per model + traffic histogram by hour; Due: 2026-01-20
Owner: Daniel Mercer; Item: Provide SOC 2 attestation + encryption practice doc and list of required controls; Due: 2026-01-19
Owner: Marco Ruiz (Redwood); Item: Run back-of-envelope sizing for reserved node counts and warm pool prewarm time based on provided traffic; Due: 2026-01-22
Owner: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE); Item: Send pricing sheet for Dedicated SKUs and hybrid burst uplift, include Dedicated vs. Private comparison; Due: 2026-01-15
next_steps: Redwood to size reserved pool and propose 3 sizing options (conservative/expected/peak)
Customer to circulate security controls and compliance requirements to Redwood SEs
Schedule 1-hr follow-up to review sizing and proposed rollout (can be demo of prewarm/fallback)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-13 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam Tran (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (Edenbridge Head of ML), Tom Reeves (Platform Eng), Daniel Mercer (Security), Priya Iyer (Product)
Recording note: partial audio drop at 00:27:30-00:28:10; rough auto-transcription, some proper nouns garbled

Summary auto: customer evaluating reserved/dedicated GPUs with hybrid burst to hosted; heavy emphasis on per-tenant isolation for high-risk models and EU data residency; wants cost/latency tradeoffs and SLA discussion

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining; i'm sophie, i'll run the commercial side and marco and liam are our SEs, how are you all?
[00:12] Aisha: hi, great, thanks. good to meet you. sorry, timezone shuffle but we're all here.
[00:18] Marco: awesome. quick agenda, we'll go through your workload shapes, isolation needs, security constraints, then sizing and burst patterns and finish with next steps. sound good?
[00:27] Tom: yep, that works. to set context, we run a mix of real-time chat summarization for customer support and batch scoring for fraud models. most of the heavy scoring jobs run in EU region, data residency is a hard requirement for certain models.
[00:42] Daniel: and from sec, we need audit logs, KMS integration with our HSM, SOC 2 plus some encryption-at-rest proofs.
[00:50] Liam: okay good to know. two quick clarifying questions — are you leaning Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private at this point? and do you have traffic patterns that are constant or spiky?
[01:05] Aisha: ideally we'd have dedicated reserved nodes for production to guarantee latency, but we'd like to burst to hosted for traffic spikes so we don't overcommit. some teams might want private on-prem for PII models later but not initially.
[01:20] Sophie: helps us a lot. what's your target P95 latency for online scoring? and cost target per token or per-embedding?
[01:30] Aisha: for our chat features p95 <= 250ms is desired; for batch fraud scoring latency is less strict but throughput is critical. Cost — across the platform we aim to average under $0.002 per token for high-throughput models; but happy to balance.
[01:46] [crosstalk] Priya: also important — different models have different owner teams and we need tenancy separation so Model A (sensitive) cannot share a GPU with Model B (external partner).
[02:00] Marco: understood. there's a couple of tenancy patterns — pure single-tenant nodes, tenant-sharding per GPU, or soft isolation with ballooning limits. given your requirement sounds like strict isolation for some models and shared capacity for others.
[02:15] Tom: yeah strict for the partner-facing models. smaller internal models can run shared. do you support node-level fencing or do we need to carve full machines?
[02:24] Marco: you can do both — dedicated physical tenancy (we call Dedicated with node reservation) or constrained multi-tenant via cgroups and tenant fencing. for highest assurance, reserved physical nodes is recommended. there's an operational tradeoff though — cost and utilization.
[02:40] Daniel: for audit we also need per-tenant access logs and token lineage, not just infra logs. is that captured?
[02:49] Liam: yes, Redwood Console logs per-request metadata (model, token counts, route, timestamp). we can push those to your syslog/SPLUNK or S3 with encryption. tiny caveat: the level of PII in payloads matters for retention policies.
[03:05] Aisha: good, can you articulate how hybrid burst works — if we have reserved nodes but traffic spikes 5x for an hour, how does the fallback to hosted look?
[03:16] Marco: two modes. fast-fallback (server-side routing) — requests overflow to Redwood hosted models in the same region; there's a routing policy that maintains routing by customer and model versions. second is prewarm pools — we can configure a warm pool of on-demand capacity that is cheaper to prewarm but still reserved. there's a small burst uplift cost for hosted overflow.
[03:36] Tom: what about cold-start and kv cache warming — we do many long-form chat convos and KV cache hit rate matters for latency.
[03:44] Marco: KV cache (auto prefix caches) persist per model if you use pinned versions; the warm pool helps keep KV in-GPU memory. if you route to hosted variants that are different quantization, you may see some jitter until the kv warms. we try to minimize that by model variant matching.
[03:59] Daniel: encryption and keys — can you integrate with our AWS KMS plus a corporate HSM? we need key rotation control too.
[04:08] Liam: yes, Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC allows you to bring your KMS keys, and we support HSM-backed keys for Signed attestations. rotation schedules are supported via our key policies. we'll need a FIFE (typo) — sorry, an encryption handshake doc exchanged.
[04:22] [00:27:30-00:28:10 audio blip — partial drop]
[04:30] Aisha: on the sizing side, our peak is often batch windows at 03:00 UTC where fraud scoring spikes, otherwise normal day chat is 3-4 rps per model cluster, with occasional product-promoted events causing short-lived spikes.
[04:45] Marco: can you share the traffic histogram by hour and 95/99 percentiles — that will let us estimate warm pool vs reserve node counts.
[04:53] Tom: yes we'll get that, action item.
[04:57] Priya: also timeline — we're looking to go live on core models in Q2, pilot with a few teams in late Q1. procurement will need committed monthlys for Dedicated.
[05:10] Sophie: procurement note — our Dedicated contracts have monthly committed units with optional burst to hosted; pricing differs by region and prewarm policy. i'll send the pricing matrix.
[05:20] Aisha: on monitoring; we need per-model SLOs and an alerting hook. do you integrate with Prometheus/Grafana?
[05:28] Liam: yes metrics exportable — token rates, p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, batch sizes. we can also emit tracing headers for request-level tracing into your APM.
[05:36] Tom: about failover — if an entire reserved rack goes down, what's typical RTO?
[05:42] Marco: depends on your redundancy — cross-zone reserved nodes plus host fallback be <5 minutes for routing but cold KV warming can add minutes to fully restore p95. if you want a 1-2 minute RTO we recommend multi-rack reserve + warm pool and automated fallback policy.
[05:58] Daniel: curious about attestation — we may need annual penetration test results and network diagrams before we sign. can you provide SOC 2 + third-party pen test reports?
[06:07] Sophie: yes. we'll share SOC 2, ISO snapshot and a redacted network diagram; detailed pen test reports often require an NDA or specific data sharing agreement.
[06:18] Aisha: any limits on model sizes for reserved? we have one very large multi-lingual model ~70B params that we'd like to host private.
[06:27] Marco: 70B is supported on our larger GPU SKUs with model sharding; for Private on-prem we'd need hardware validation but Dedicated can host that in EU region — quantization/partitions are options to reduce memory.
[06:40] [slight overlap] Tom: cost ask — can you do committed consumption discounts and how do you bill for burst?
[06:48] Sophie: committed pricing has tiered discounts by commit level; burst to hosted is billed at a higher per-token rate for overflow plus a small routing fee. we'll include examples in the pricing sheet.
[06:58] Marco: one more operational note — we recommend a canary rollout per model and a rollback policy; Redwood Console supports canary percentages and automatic fallback if quality/regression alerts fire. helpful for you given many teams owning models.
[07:12] Priya: that sounds good. any competitors we should be aware of for dedicated?
[07:16] Daniel: we've been talking to OtherCloudAI and Infrakit, both offer reserved GPUs but their VPC isolation story is weaker.
[07:25] Sophie: thanks — good to know.
[07:28] Marco: okay, quick recap of open items: customer shares traffic histograms and model list with owners, security sends SOC2 + controls doc, redwood runs sizing and sends pricing + reserved vs private comparison, and we'll schedule follow-up.
[07:43] Aisha: correct. one question — is there a self-serve pilot to test prewarm times?
[07:49] Marco: yes we can do a short pilot with a small reserved pool and synthetic spike tests; usually 2-4 weeks to get meaningful telemetry.
[07:57] Sophie: i'll propose dates in the follow-up email. any final questions?
[08:02] Tom: none from me. thanks all.
[08:05] Daniel: no, thanks.
[08:07] Sophie: great, we'll follow up with docs and sizing by next week. talk soon.

End of transcript.
